questions.q: What are the two fundamental kinds of transaction source in Receivables?
questions.explain: Every transaction source is either Manual (for transactions keyed in directly) or Imported (used exclusively for AutoInvoice-fed transactions).

questions.q: Can you manually key a transaction against an Imported transaction source?
options: Yes, Imported sources work identically to Manual sources
No — Imported sources exist purely to support the AutoInvoice interface
questions.explain: Imported sources are reserved for AutoInvoice; they are not available for direct manual transaction entry.

questions.q: Which of the following is something a transaction source controls?
options: The company's chart of accounts structure
questions.explain: Transaction sources control numbering sequences, how dates are derived (especially for imports), type defaulting, and validation strictness.

questions.q: In the Northwind Fixtures Co. example, why did AR Manual Entry and OM AutoInvoice Import use different numbering ranges?
options: Because Oracle Fusion requires random numbering
Because credit memos always need a separate range
So anyone reviewing a batch could tell at a glance which transactions were keyed in manually versus imported automatically
questions.explain: Giving each source its own numbering range makes the origin of a transaction visible just from its number, which is a common and deliberate setup choice.

questions.q: Together with transaction type, what does transaction source help determine?
options: The level of control (how much review is required) before a transaction can complete
The company's fiscal year end date
The language of the printed invoice only
questions.explain: The combination of transaction source and transaction type determines how strict completion requirements are — tighter for manual entry, looser for trusted automated imports.
